biography.plain_text: Don C. Bedell is an American healthcare entrepreneur and conservationist from Sikeston, Missouri. He founded and ran numerous companies, chiefly in nursing-home and healthcare management, and remains chairman of Castle Partners. Bedell also served two terms on the Missouri Conservation Commission, chairing the body and helping oversee the state's wildlife and habitat programmes.

long_biography.plain_text:
Childhood summers with his grandparents on Missouri's Current River gave Don C. Bedell an early attachment to fishing and the outdoors. He later studied agriculture and animal nutrition before building a business career in healthcare. His conservation work grew through sustained support of wildlife organisations and state service.

Bedell spent two terms on the Missouri Conservation Commission, eventually serving as chair. His tenure included the restoration of elk to the state, and Missouri later named a 5,805-acre unit of the Peck Ranch Conservation Area for him. The protected woodland recognises contributions that continued well beyond his commercial work.
